title: Ibovespa Hits Record High on Election Polls
body: The Ibovespa climbed 1.4% on Friday to a record close of 209,067 points, after the first post–first-round voting-intention polls confirmed Flávio Bolsonaro's lead over President Lula in the runoff. Investors tend to view Bolsonaro as more fiscally conservative, reinforcing expectations that a potential administration would tighten control over public spending and improve Brazil's fiscal outlook. Even so, the race remains highly competitive, with some polls indicating a statistical tie. Financial stocks largely advanced: Itaú gained 2.3%, while Banco do Brasil (BB) and Itaúsa each rose 1.6%, and B3 added 2.5%. Petrobras edged up 0.9% despite swings in international oil prices. Vale erased earlier losses late in the session and closed 0.38% higher, trading in a tight range after iron ore prices hit multi-month lows. Retail names posted strong gains as bond yields fell in the wake of the polls, even against a backdrop of accelerating inflation and an inflation print above the upper bound of the Brazilian Central Bank's target range. Magazine Luiza jumped 19.2%. For the week, the Ibovespa advanced 8.82%, marking its strongest weekly performance of 2026. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: TSX Gains on BoC Rate-Hold Bets
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index climbed 1.5% to close at 35,665 on Friday, as weaker labour market data reinforced expectations that the Bank of Canada will hold off on further interest rate increases. Canadian employment declined by 68,300, sharply missing forecasts for a 7,000 gain, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 6.5%, in line with expectations. The data pushed government bond yields lower, providing support for credit-sensitive equities. Major banks advanced, with Royal Bank of Canada up 1.1%, Toronto-Dominion Bank gaining 1.2%, Bank of Montreal rising 1.6%, and both Bank of Nova Scotia and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce adding 1.3%. Gold prices also moved higher, boosting mining shares. Agnico Eagle climbed 3.2%, while Barrick Gold and Wheaton Precious Metals each added 2.9%. Lundin Mining surged 10.5% after its Fruta del Norte mine in Ecuador reported its strongest production quarter on record. Energy producers advanced despite choppy crude oil trading. Technology stocks also gained, supported by strength in US hyperscalers, with Shopify rising 4.1%. In the consumer space, Aritzia soared 20.5% after reporting second-quarter revenue and earnings that exceeded expectations. For the week, the TSX finished up 0.9%. title: Oil Wavers on Potential Russian Diesel Release
body: Crude prices hovered around $91.50 a barrel on Friday after US President Trump announced that Russian President Putin had agreed to release diesel supplies onto the global market. The US Treasury Department said the Office of Foreign Assets Control was "immediately issuing a temporary general license" to permit Russian diesel exports, with the proposed volume estimated at about 22.5 million barrels. At the same time, the US-Iran conflict has disrupted shipping. A substantial portion of the tanker fleet is currently engaged in ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, driving global freight rates to record highs and limiting vessel availability on other routes. Eleven tankers were attacked while transiting Hormuz during the week ended October 4. Earlier this week, Trump said he would not order another strike on Iran before the November midterm elections, citing what he called productive talks with Tehran. Over the week, oil prices registered a gain of roughly 0.2%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Rise on Earnings Optimism
body: US stock indices ended higher on Friday, supported by expectations for a strong earnings season. The S&P 500 gained 0.6% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.5%, leaving both benchmarks close to their record highs, while the Dow advanced 423 points. Broad-based strength in corporate results has been a key driver of equity performance this year. Wall Street's biggest banks are projected to report nearly $19 billion in stock-trading revenue when they release quarterly earnings next week. Goldman Sachs (+1.4%), which reports on Tuesday, is expected to deliver $5.1 billion, followed by Morgan Stanley (+1.4%) with an estimated $4.9 billion. JPMorgan (+0.5%) is forecast to post $4.5 billion, and Bank of America (+1.4%) is projected to generate $2.6 billion. AI-focused hyperscalers advanced on optimism that OpenAI's annualized revenue could surpass $70 billion by year-end. Alphabet climbed 1%, Microsoft gained 2.4% and Amazon rose 3.3%. For the week, the S&P 500 added 0.9%, the Nasdaq slipped 0.1% and the Dow increased by 585 points. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Mexican Peso Weakens Toward One-Year Low
body: The Mexican peso weakened to about 18.44 per US dollar in October, approaching a one‑year low following the release of the Bank of Mexico's meeting minutes. The currency became one of the worst performers among emerging markets, as the minutes kept open the prospect of additional interest-rate cuts. Most members of the Governing Board indicated that moderating core inflation and subdued domestic consumption create scope to continue easing monetary policy through late 2026 and into early 2027. This reinforced expectations of a narrowing interest-rate differential between Mexico and the United States, diminishing the peso's attractiveness for carry trades and driving stronger demand for dollars in the spot market. Meanwhile, annual inflation accelerated to 3.45% in September from 3.26% in August. Although slightly below market forecasts, the figure added uncertainty to the outlook for domestic monetary policy.
